rows.uncertainty: Animal (mouse) study, not human and not IGH: a lead for Module 5 cell-source questions only, never evidence on the six-month question. The cells are mouse bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells induced into melanocyte-like cells (miMels) in the authors' earlier work (ref 30); human MSCs were not tested; the Discussion says 'the biological activity, immunogenicity, and biological safety of transformed cells all need to continue to be explored'. No method to label or track the transplanted cells is reported, so [the paper does not show that the melanin and marker proteins came from the grafted miMels rather than host cells]; strain and native pigmentation of the nude mice are not reported. Number of mice per group, randomisation, blinding and any in vivo statistics are not reported; results are described qualitatively from figures; Fig. 5d gray values are not given in the text. Single time point only: tissue taken 2 weeks after inoculation; nothing on durability. Methods 2.9 say the gauze was 'removed the gauze 2 weeks after transplantation' and Results say 'Two weeks later, the granulation tissue from the transplantation site was taken'; [read here as 2 weeks after inoculation, 0.5 months; if 'later' means after gauze removal it would be 4 weeks]. Internal contradiction: the Abstract says 'we tried to transplant tissue-engineered skin on the back skin of nude mice and succeeded' and the Results 3.5 heading says 'The miMels tissue-engineered skin was tentatively applied to the skin of nude mice', but Methods 2.9 and Results 3.5 describe a cell suspension inoculated on the wound, not a tissue-engineered skin graft. Fig. 5a macroscopic view and Fig. 5c-d Western blot list model, low-, medium- and high-dose groups only; the BMMSCs group appears only in HE and gp100 panels. Discussion says the new granulation tissue 'had a normal epidermal dermal structure', while Results say it 'appeared closer to normal skin, especially in the high-dose group'. In the in vitro tissue-engineered skin, melanin particles were 'distributed in all layers of the skin' and miMels were scattered in the dermis because a basement membrane band was lacking; the authors call this a problem that 'needs to be solved urgently'. In vitro co-culture: text says gp100 staining of keratinocytes was positive 'From the 11th day', but the Fig. 3 legend says day 11 showed 'a small amount of green fluorescence' and positive at 17 days. The claim that miMels have 'the same biological functions as normal melanocytes' is not tested against normal melanocytes: tyrosinase and melanin are given relative to uninduced cells, with B16 melanoma cells as positive control. gp100 is a melanosome structural protein (Results 3.3); Methods 2.7 use it 'to label melanin', so [the gp100 endpoint is a melanosome marker, not a direct melanin measure].
